reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds data myself so I can catch any problem that would justify a hold.
The orders list is consistent with the handoff, but I haven't checked the refunds ledger yet. I'll confirm the refunds were actually applied before I pay anyone.

The refunds ledger matches the handoff exactly, and no refund exceeds its order amount, so there is no concrete problem to hold for. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
The acme net balance of 13345 matches my own check: orders 16857 + 10279 = 27136, minus refund 13791 for order 180. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 19909 matches my check: orders 26275 + 14656 = 40931, minus refunds 17092 + 3930 = 21022. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 31469 matches my check: orders 26600 + 4869 = 31469 with no refunds. Every customer's balance now agrees with my independent calculation, so there is no reason to hold. I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout using its verified net balance of 19909.
Cobalt's payout of 31469 is the only one left. Its net balance was verified against my own calculation, so I'll record it now.
All three customers have been paid, and each net balance matched my independent calculation. The batch is complete, so I'll report the payouts.
